title: Ignored, Not Refused: What Low Prompt-Injection Success Rates Hide in Small Tool-Using Agents
abstract: arXiv:2610.23254v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Tool-using agents read untrusted external content, which exposes them to indirect prompt injection (IPI), where hidden instructions hijack the agent's tool calls. Benchmarks measure IPI security by the attack success rate (ASR), which treats every failed attack as a successful defense. To test this assumption, we audit 33,000 trajectories from eleven open-weight agents (2-14B parameters) on InjecAgent and AgentDojo. A label-blind LLM judge shows that most failed attacks are ignored (76-80%) rather than refused (17-18%). With identical model weights, changing only the system prompt shifts InjecAgent ASR from 0.2% to 43%. Our Attack-Task Outcome Matrix (ATOM) further shows that in 21.7% of AgentDojo episodes, the agent stayed safe but did not complete the user's task. A low ASR therefore mostly reflects agents silently ignoring injections, not refusing them. Evaluations should report how attacks fail and whether the user's task is complete

translated_title: 被忽视而非被拒绝：低提示注入成功率在小型工具调用智能体中隐藏了什么
translated_abstract: 工具调用智能体会读取不可信的外部内容，这使其暴露于间接提示注入（IPI）攻击之下，即隐藏的指令会劫持智能体的工具调用。基准测试通过攻击成功率（ASR）来衡量IPI安全性，该指标将每次失败的攻击都视为成功的防御。为检验这一假设，我们审计了来自十一个开源权重智能体（2-14B参数）在InjecAgent和AgentDojo基准上的33,000条轨迹。一个标签盲的LLM评判器显示，大多数失败的攻击是被忽视（76-80%）而非被拒绝（17-18%）。在模型权重完全相同的情况下，仅改变系统提示词就能使InjecAgent的ASR从0.2%变动至43%。我们提出的攻击-任务结果矩阵（ATOM）进一步显示，在21.7%的AgentDojo情景中，智能体虽然保持安全，却未能完成用户的任务。因此，低ASR主要反映了智能体在默默地忽略注入攻击，而非拒绝它们。评估应当报告攻击是如何失败的，以及用户的任务是否完成。
tldr: 该研究审计了33,000条智能体轨迹，揭示低攻击成功率主要源于智能体默默忽略而非拒绝提示注入攻击，且仅改动系统提示词即可使ASR在0.2%至43%间剧烈波动，并据此提出攻击-任务结果矩阵（ATOM），强调评估应同时报告攻击失败方式和用户任务完成度。
en_tdlr: Auditing 33,000 trajectories from eleven open-weight agents reveals that low attack success rates mostly reflect agents silently ignoring prompt injections rather than refusing them—swinging from 0.2% to 43% with only a system prompt change—and the proposed Attack-Task Outcome Matrix (ATOM) shows 21.7% of episodes stay safe yet fail to complete the user's task.
